_README: EQLS Auras is Shara's project. Shara has creative and production control over it and her copy reaches this file through the owner. NOTHING IN HERE MAY BE WRITTEN BY A BUILD SESSION. lede and body[0] are her Pitch section from HIGHLIGHTS.md, verbatim, replacing text from the product's first version that was still live on launch day and described roughly a hundredth of what it now does. Faithful transport preserved an obsolete claim perfectly, which is why this file names its source: point it at the current one when she updates it.
name: EQLS Auras
lede: A countdown timer for every buff you’re running, right on top of the game. Read straight from your EverQuest Legends log.
body: EQLS Auras watches your log while you play and puts a click-through overlay on screen with a timer for every buff you’re running. Build as many overlays as you want, put them where you want, give them sounds. Point an aura at any line in your log, not just buffs the app knows. It hides when you tab out of EQ and comes back when you tab in. It tracks your weekly raid lockouts, which EQ never prints.

It reads files the client already has: the log it writes as you play, your spellbook, and the game’s own spell icons. It does not read or alter the game’s memory, inject code into it, or send it input. It fetches its typeface from Google each time it launches, which discloses your IP address to Google; beyond that it sends nothing — no telemetry, no analytics, no update check. That fetch is the main window only: the overlay drawn over the game requests nothing at all.
The idea is WeakAuras’. The code is not: a from-scratch implementation for EverQuest Legends, sharing no code and no trigger format with it, and neither affiliated with nor endorsed by its authors.

It was, with object-fit:cover, and that silently cropped anything not 16:9 - auras-list-aura is 322x408 PORTRAIT and would have lost roughly four fifths of itself, which is the image that carries her 'icon grid or list' claim. Each figure now takes its own intrinsic ratio from media.json's w/h, so a portrait still stays portrait. Adding one still moves no layout: the grid is auto-fit and rows size themselves.

subs: Add overlays and put them where you want. Point an aura at any line in your log, not just buffs the app knows. It shows what you have landed on each groupmate, skins your action bar, routes you across the map, and tracks the weekly raid lockouts EQ never prints. One key hides the lot.

It reads files the client already has: the log it writes as you play, your spellbook, and the game’s own spell icons. It does not read or alter the game’s memory, inject code into it, or send it input. No telemetry, no analytics, no update check.
band.foot: Free. It finds your EverQuest install on its own. Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher — More info, then Run anyway.
band._figures: EMPTIED 5 Sep 2026, and the reason is the useful part. This carried four figures with the best provenance in the repository - each naming its file, its field, its verifier and its date. TWO OF THE FOUR WERE STALE WITHIN TWO DAYS. '1,067 spells known' was the raw entry count of buffs.json, but src/main/buffStore.js:51 drops durationSec > MAX_TRACKABLE_DURATION_SEC (5*3600), so the app loads 1,066 - one entry, 'Share Form of the Great Wolf' at 21600s. I verified 1,067 myself on 3 Sep and I measured the FILE while the label said 'spells known'. '53 stacking slots' is 56 now. A PROVENANCE RECORD ANSWERS WHERE A FIGURE CAME FROM AND CANNOT ANSWER WHETHER IT IS STILL TRUE. The rule this repo now applies: publish a figure with a guard, or stop publishing it. THE BUILD CANNOT GUARD THESE - they live in another repository and the build has no network - so the only honest options were a vendored snapshot carrying a visible read-date, as assets/50-upgrades.json does, or silence. Silence today; the snapshot is the better answer and is not a thing to build the weekend before a relaunch. Derivations if they ever return: buffs.json minus that filter -> 1,066; `headings` in buff-lines.json -> 56; `ZONES` in zoneGraph.js -> 104; audio under sounds/ excluding LICENSE.txt -> 15.

lines.lead: Every buff you’re running, counting down, on top of the game.
lines.rest: Read straight from your live log.

lines.lead: As many auras as you want, each its own window.
lines.rest: Position, size, opacity, colours and text, set per aura and remembered.
Switch any aura between the two.
Click-through, so it never eats a click. Hides when EQ isn’t the focused window, comes straight back when it is.

lines.lead: See what you’ve cast on your group.
lines.rest: Shows what’s landed on each groupmate, by name.
Buff timers, cooldown timers, resist flashes, “you got dispelled,” “your charm broke.” Drop them in, done.

lines.lead: A cooldown timer that tracks the buff first.
lines.rest: One tile counts the buff down, then rolls straight into “ready in X” with no reset.

lines.lead: Trigger an aura off any log line.
lines.rest: Cast lines, zone in and out, or any text you type.
AND/OR several triggers on one aura. Or invert an aura so it shows what hasn’t happened yet — “this is ready, go use it.”
A fixed label the moment a trigger fires, no timer.

lines.lead: Share an aura with a code.
lines.rest: Copy the config to a short code, a friend pastes it in and has the same aura.

lines.lead: Separate sounds for landed, expiring and expired.
lines.rest: Per aura.
Any audio file on your PC. Starter sounds ship with the app.
EQ never prints a lockout line, so the app reads the weekly-task messages it does print on a kill and tracks each lockout from those.
Pick where you’re going, get the route across 100+ zones and the travel spell for each step.
Overlay tiles that sit on your real action bar buttons — game spell icons, hybrid icons that combine two, or plain frames. Per profile. Doesn’t touch the real bar.
A sound the moment someone opens a trade with you.
Splits your log per day and per session, archives at each raid reset, plus a manual archive-and-truncate. Your raw log folder stops growing forever.

lines.lead: Fix the spell data by hand.
lines.rest: Browse every spell the app knows, correct a wrong one, or add your own. Your fix sticks through updates.

lines.lead: Move your setup to another PC.
lines.rest: Export every aura, profile, sound and setting to a folder, import it on the other machine. Offline.

steps: Windows SmartScreen will warn about an unknown publisher. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
Open EQLS Auras. It finds your EverQuest install on its own — nothing to point it at.
